## 02 — Selected work

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/projects/attendance-dark.svg">
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/projects/attendance-light.svg">
  <img alt="Smart Attendance (2026, Team of two). Face or rotating-QR attendance that a photo on a phone cannot fool. 25–34× faster on GPU. Pipeline: BlazeFace (in the browser) → Detect (SCRFD on GPU) → ArcFace (512-d match) → Liveness (4 checks + 2 models) → Record (integrity score); Liveness loop: 3 frames in a row · any fail resets. Problem: Roll calls and sign-in sheets are easy to proxy, and a face held up on a phone is still a face. Key idea: A match only counts after liveness passes on three frames in a row: four OpenCV checks run in parallel with two MiniFASNet models. My part: Backend, recognition and anti-spoofing pipeline, analytics and benchmarks. A teammate built the QR flow. Stack: Django, PostgreSQL, InsightFace, ONNX Runtime, OpenCV, React." src="assets/projects/attendance-light.svg" width="100%">
</picture>

<a href="https://github.com/ganesan33/AcentraHealth">

  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/projects/fraud-agent-dark.svg">
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/projects/fraud-agent-light.svg">
  <img alt="Fraud investigation agent (2026, Team of three). An LLM investigates disputed payments; a rule engine makes the call. R1–R10 rules decide. Pipeline: Traverse (TigerGraph hops) → Evidence (case-scoped) → LLM (proposes) → Rules (R1–R10 decide) → Verdict (SAR + audit). Problem: Analysts piece fraud cases together by hand from cards, devices, regions and earlier cases. Key idea: The model never gets the last word: deterministic policy rules set the verdict, so every outcome traces to a named rule. My part: The first FastAPI backend, and the R1–R10 rule engine with its registry and unit tests. Stack: Python, FastAPI, TigerGraph, Groq, React, TypeScript." src="assets/projects/fraud-agent-light.svg" width="100%">
</picture>
</a>

<a href="https://github.com/ganesan33/eduflow">
<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/projects/eduflow-dark.svg">
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/projects/eduflow-light.svg">
  <img alt="EduFlow (2025–26, Solo). A course platform that turned out to be mostly a video problem. 3 repos, built solo. Pipeline: Upload (Express 5 · Joi) → Queue (BullMQ on Redis) → Worker (ffmpeg, own process) → Blob (source + MP4) → Player (HTTP range); Worker loop: up to 3 tries · exponential backoff. Problem: Course videos are large: processing them inside a web request is slow and fragile, yet playback must seek instantly. Key idea: Uploads go onto a queue; a separate ffmpeg worker transcodes, retries with backoff and records each video’s status. My part: All of it: React web app, Node API, Kotlin Android client, Azure DevOps pipeline to App Service. Stack: Node.js, Express, MongoDB, Redis, React, Kotlin, Azure." src="assets/projects/eduflow-light.svg" width="100%">
</picture>
</a>

<p align="right"><sub><a href="https://github.com/ganesan33/eduflow">Web ↗</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp; <a href="https://github.com/ganesan33/backend-">API v2 ↗</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp; <a href="https://github.com/ganesan33/Eduflow-Mobile-app">Android ↗</a></sub></p>
